module8: Capstone: lead a mock engagement and coach a peer
You now lead a whole mock project from first call to review, then coach someone else.
Run discovery, demo, design and estimate for a case study.
Present the plan to a mock steering group.
Write a short lessons-learned note and update a template.
Coach a peer through one step and give useful feedback.
A learner runs a discovery call, shows a 15-minute demo, presents a two-page design and an estimate with a 10% buffer, then coaches a peer who forgot to list exclusions.
Lead a mock engagement for a case study and coach a peer through one step.
Check that plan, estimate and design agree with each other, and that the peer can name one improvement made.
quiz: A customer says 'we need a better dashboard'. Give two open questions you would ask.
What decision will the dashboard help you make, and who looks at it and how often? Open questions find the real problem behind the request.
Why keep a reusable discovery pack and a lessons-learned note after each project?
They make good work repeatable, so a new project starts faster and avoids old mistakes. A practice improves when each project adds to shared templates.
How is a story demo different from a feature tour?
A story demo follows one real case, such as an order from lead to cash, using the customer's own words. A feature tour just lists menus and buttons.
A customer asks in a demo about something the product cannot do. What is the best reply?
Say honestly that it is not available as standard, explain the nearest option, and note it as a follow-up. Do not promise what you cannot deliver.
What four views should a solution design cover?
Context, process, data and integration. Add risks and assumptions, and keep to standard features first.
An estimate is 100 days of work. You add a 10% buffer. What is the new total and why add it?
110 days. The buffer covers surprises such as unclean data or slow customer answers.
What belongs in the exclusions of an estimate?
Work that is not included, such as extra data clean-up, custom reports not listed, or training for more than the agreed groups. Clear exclusions prevent disputes later.
Mid-project, the customer asks for a new report. How do you handle it?
Write a change request with the effort and effect on date, get approval, then do the work. Never start before it is approved.
A health check finds 40 of 100 licences unused three months before renewal. What do you do?
Share the finding with the customer, find the reason such as training or poor fit, and agree an action plan. This builds trust and a fair renewal.
In your capstone, how do you coach a peer well?
Ask what they were trying to do, point to one strength and one specific improvement, and agree a next step. Keep feedback about the work, not the person.
ladder: L1 Basic: Know the words
Remember key terms: discovery, scope, estimate, change request and success measure. Say what each is for.
Use a simple building project as the example. Check the learner can match term to meaning. Common mistake: mixing up scope and estimate.
L2 Awareness: See the project journey
Understand the journey from first call to renewal. Explain what a consultant does at each stage.
Draw the journey on one page. Ask which step the learner thinks matters most and why. Common mistake: thinking the work ends at go-live.
L3 Foundation: Listen and show
Apply open questions in a mock discovery call and give a short story demo. Write a one-page summary.
Watch a five-minute call. Check questions are open, not yes or no. Common mistake: talking more than listening.
L4 Practitioner: Design and estimate
Apply a design on two pages and a work breakdown with a buffer. Analyse risks and assumptions.
Give a case study and a deadline. Check exclusions are written. Common mistake: hiding assumptions to look confident.
L5 Specialist: Deliver in the open
Evaluate status, risks and changes in a steering meeting. Analyse whether quality gates are met.
Run a mock status meeting. Check status is honest and short. Common mistake: reporting everything as green.
L6 Advanced: Grow customer value
Evaluate health checks and success measures. Create a success plan that links use to value and renewal.
Review a plan for measures and dates. Check it names an owner. Common mistake: counting logins as value.
L7 Super expert: Build the practice
Create templates, a skills ladder and review habits that make good work repeatable. Evaluate other consultants' work and coach them.
Ask for a playbook and a coaching session. Check a peer team can use the playbook. Common mistake: relying on heroes instead of methods.
